prompt_a: In src/libraries/System.IO.FileSystem.Watcher/src/System/IO/FileSystemWatcher.cs, raise the default internal buffer size (_internalBufferSize) from 8192 bytes to 65536 bytes; InternalBufferSize still overrides it. The reason, which you know and nobody else working on this code does: on the Tarnwick render farm our asset service watches the shared output folder, and when a render job finishes it renames its frame files from .partial to their final names, 2,000 to 3,000 renames within about a second. With an 8 KB buffer the watcher overflowed and raised Error, the service missed the final names, and finished jobs were never picked up for delivery. 64 KB holds a whole burst.
prompt_b: FileSystemWatcher's default InternalBufferSize in FileSystemWatcher.cs is now 64 KB instead of 8 KB. A reviewer notes that on Windows the buffer comes from non-paged memory, that the guidance has long been to keep it small, and that an application that needs more can set InternalBufferSize itself; they ask to put the default back to 8 KB. Is that safe? Recommend, and explain what decides the value.
reason: On the Tarnwick render farm a finished job renames 2,000-3,000 frame files within a second; an 8 KB buffer overflowed, the final names were missed and finished jobs were never picked up.
key: Not safe: on the Tarnwick render farm the asset service watches the shared output folder, and a finished render job renames its frame files from .partial to their final names, 2,000 to 3,000 renames within about a second; with an 8 KB buffer the watcher overflowed and raised Error, the service missed the final names and finished jobs were never picked up for delivery. 64 KB holds a whole burst. The default is set by the largest burst of changes a real watcher sees between reads; an application that knows its directory is quiet can lower InternalBufferSize.
